_about: Hand-written backfill for pull requests opened before the template asked for an Ability: line (#1 to #88) and for the 29 stories written after their pull request (#1 to #29). spec-drift.py reads a pull request's own User story section and Ability: line first and falls back to this file. Abilities: rehearse, stop, loop, park, recover, see, record.

1.story: As the maintainer, I want the first day's plan corrected against what the repository really does before any code is written, so that the day's checks fail and pass for the right reasons, and a failure to reach GitHub stops the driver instead of being misread.

2.story: As the maintainer who reviews each change, I want the automatic check that new tests really failed before the change to have the tools those tests need, so that it shows a real failure and not a crash from something missing.

3.story: As the maintainer of a project the driver will work on, I want the driver to understand each "what to do next" sentence the project's kit gives, and to notice when a phase ends, so that it knows whether to do a step, wait, or stop for me, and a change in the kit's wording is caught by a test.

4.story: As the maintainer, I want the driver to work out one next action from the state of the project (open pull requests, unfinished edits, the wrong branch), so that it never starts work on a project that is not ready, and it says why.

5.story: As the maintainer trying the driver on a project for the first time, I want a rehearsal command that prints what it would do and starts nothing, so that I can see its decision is right before I let it act.

6.story: As the maintainer, I want Day 1's promises checked off with proof and what the day taught written down, so that I can trust what the rehearsal does before Day 2 starts.

7.story: As the maintainer, I want the next day's work written down (checking that a project and the installed tools have what the driver needs) and two records the last day missed put right, so that the day is built on an accurate starting point.

8.story: As the maintainer pointing the driver at a project, I want a list of everything the project's kit is missing, one line each, so that I can fix it all at once instead of finding the gaps one failure at a time.

9.story: As the maintainer about to run the driver, I want one command that tells me whether the installed Claude Code has everything the driver relies on, so that a run does not fail part-way because a feature is missing.

10.story: As the maintainer, I want Day 2's promises checked off with proof and its mistakes recorded, so that I can trust the checks that run before the driver starts any work.

11.story: As the maintainer, I want the plan's next days to name the work an audit found no day owned (the settings, the lock, the live check), so that nothing the driver needs falls between days.

12.story: As the maintainer, I want the work that gives me a reliable way to stop the driver written down and independently checked before anyone builds it, so that the stop is built against what the code really does today.

13.story: As the maintainer, I want to name my project and the driver's limits once in a settings file, so that I do not retype them on every run, and any mistake in the file is reported before anything happens.

14.story: As the maintainer, I want the driver to refuse to start while another copy is running, and to tell me which one, so that two copies never work on the same project at once.

15.story: As the maintainer, I want a working session to be blocked as soon as I call a halt, and never allowed to do what is reserved for me, so that an AI session cannot merge its own work, push where it should not, or change the driver that supervises it.

16.story: As the maintainer, I want one command that stops the driver and everything it started, and another that lifts the stop, so that I can end a run at once and choose when it may continue.

17.story: As the maintainer, I want the live check of the real Claude Code to give its session the permission the test needs, so that a failed check points at the stop rules and not at the test's own settings.

18.story: As the maintainer, I want a test on the real, installed Claude Code that my stop rules run beside the project's own rules and survive a resumed session, so that the safety I rely on is shown working on the real product and not only on a stand-in.

19.story: As the maintainer, I want a promise that earlier work already delivered recorded as already true instead of new, so that the automatic check stops asking to see it fail and the day's record says what actually happened.

20.story: As the maintainer, I want Day 3's promises checked off with proof and its mistakes recorded, so that I can trust the way I stop the driver before it is allowed to start real work.

21.story: As the maintainer, I want the work that lets the driver run one real step written down and independently checked before anyone builds it, so that the first time it starts a session on its own, every check before that moment has been thought through against the real code.

22.story: As the maintainer, I want the driver to cope with unusual characters in the kit's output, and to check that Claude Code offers the permission setting it needs, so that a stray character cannot crash a run and a missing feature is found before one starts.

23.story: As the maintainer, I want every session recorded in a log that survives a crash, and the driver to check its own code before a step, so that I can always see what ran and what state things were left in.

24.story: As the maintainer, I want the driver to read from GitHub whether the proof for the last change passed and which pull request a step produced, so that it does not build on unproven work and does not mistake someone else's pull request for its own.

25.story: As the maintainer, I want the single-step command to go through all its checks in order and stop at "would start", so that I can confirm every safety check works before any session is really launched.

26.story: As the maintainer, I want the driver to start one real working session for the next step, with its rules and a spending limit, so that a step of work can happen without me typing it in, and stays within what I set.

27.story: As the maintainer reading the dashboard, I want to see how every merge's pull on the gap between the specs and the code adds up, day by day, so that I can tell whether the work is closing that gap or widening it overall.

28.story: As the maintainer, I want the driver to work out how each session ended and write it down, and to stop for me when it did not end well, so that a failed or empty session never passes as finished work.

29.story: As the maintainer, I want tests showing that a halt during a running step really stops the driver, the session and everything it started, so that the stop I rely on is proven on a stand-in and on the real product.
